sources.note: Bibliographic only: two references (Elkins 1974 overview/comparative; ISO CR 2009-056); no grammar, sketch, phonology or dictionary of the language is recorded. Larena et al. 2021 (PNAS) is population genetics and was not pursued.

sources.citation: Elkins, Richard E. 1973. A preliminary Proto-Manobo word list. Philippine Journal of Linguistics 4(1) (SIL typescript copy from zorc.net)
sources.note: Not applicable: covers eight Manobo languages (TIG, BKD, SAR, WBM, ILN, DIB, CTM, TSY); Kinamigin was added only in the 1974 version.

sources.citation: Reid, Lawrence A. (ed.). 1971. Philippine minor languages: word lists and phonologies. Oceanic Linguistics Special Publication 8 (language roster checked via R. D. Zorc's list !Reid=PML=LANGUAGES.rtf)
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: open copy online: WID Old Widener Philol 961.5 no.8 (also: hathitrust digitized, search-only (in copyright))
sources.note: Not applicable: Kinamigin is not among the 43 languages in Reid 1971 (Manobo lects covered are Ata, Dibabawon, Ilianen, Sarangani, Western Bukidnon, Kalamansig Cotabato, Tigwa, Obo).

sources.citation: Gasing, Mae-Ann & Mohammad Ali Al-Saggaf. 2025. An archival study on the linguistic state of Obo Manobo and Kinamiging Manobo. Southeastern Philippines Journal of Research and Development 30(2): 165-183. DOI 10.53899/spjrd.v30i2.1041
sources.note: Nothing for Kinamiging. Its Kinamiging 'Phonology' paragraph (p. 176-177) only restates the Elkins 1974 reflex rules (16 consonants, 4 vowels; r > l and l-deletion between vowels, y > dz, *e > u). Conclusion (p. 178): 'Only one phonological study (Elkins, 1974) was identified' and the only lexical sources are Elkins & Regier 1973 and Elkins 1974. The sentence 'Word stress is placed on penultimate syllables' (p. 174) is about Obo Manobo, citing Olofson 2007, not this language.

sources.citation: Alamillo, John Brian & Ismael Talili. 2016. Language patterns and attitudes of Kinamiging Manobo speakers. JPAIR Multidisciplinary Research 26(1): 16-35. DOI 10.7719/jpair.v26i1.414
sources.note: Nothing; sociolinguistic survey of 40 speakers in Sagay, Camiguin (domains, attitudes, matched guise). No linguistic description and no prior descriptive works cited.

sources.citation: Blust, Robert. 2013. The Austronesian languages (revised ed.). Canberra: Asia-Pacific Linguistics
sources.note: Nothing for this language; Kinamigin appears only in the Manobo subgroup listing and language index.

sources.citation: Lobel, Jason William. 2013. Philippine and North Bornean languages: issues in description, subgrouping, and reconstruction. PhD dissertation, University of Hawai'i at Manoa
sources.note: Nothing for Kinamiging. Lists Kinamiging among 'previously-undocumented languages' documented during his fieldwork (p. 3) and mentions it in passing (Camiguin as one of two off-Mindanao Manobo languages, p. 24; loss of *j/*d reflexes in functors, fn. 17 p. 246; heavy Bisayan borrowing, p. 364); no Kinamiging phonology or stress data in the dissertation.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2009. Change request 2009-056 (Bill Hall, SIL Philippines; supporter Jason Lobel): rename [mkx] Manobo, Cinamiguin to Manobo, Kinamiging (adopted 2010-01-18)
sources.note: Nothing; only states that 'Cinamiguin' is an exonym that does not reflect the pronunciation; source of information = Jason Lobel's first-hand fieldwork.

sources.citation: Yap, Fe Aldave. 1977. A comparative study of Philippine lexicons. Manila: Institute of National Language. 464 pp.
sources.note: Nothing. 400-item list in 80 languages including 'Kinamigin (Kam.), Camiguin Islands'; methodology says 'The lexicons were written in phonetic orthography' and the sampled entry pages carry no stress or accent marks; the 'Phoneme inventory of 80 Philippine languages' table gives Kinamigin 21 phonemes (4 vowels) with no suprasegmentals. (Part Two, the phonological analysis, was left unpublished.)

sources.citation: Zorc, R. David. 1977. The Bisayan dialects of the Philippines: subgrouping and reconstruction. Pacific Linguistics C-44
sources.note: Nothing for this language; only notes (sec. 2.2) that Camiguin has Kinamigin, a Manobo language (Elkins 1974), which has borrowed from its Bisayan neighbours. No Kinamigin data.

sources.citation: Elkins, Richard E. 1974. A Proto-Manobo word list. Oceanic Linguistics 13(1/2): 601-641. DOI 10.2307/3622754
sources.note: Nothing. Kinamigin (KIN) is one of 12 daughter languages in a 197-item comparative list with Proto-Manobo phoneme reflex/realization rules (sec. 3-4); orthography follows SIL practical spellings; no stress or accent is marked or discussed; the gemination note (sec. 5) concerns Cagayano, Tagabawa and Obo, not Kinamigin. Acknowledges Estela L. Dagaraga (Xavier University) and Douglas Regier for the Kinamigin data (n.1, p. 638).

sources.citation: Elkins, Richard E. 1984. An extended Proto-Manobo wordlist. In Andrew Gonzalez (ed.), Panagani: essays in honor of Bonifacio P. Sibayan on his sixty-seventh birthday, 218-229. Manila: Linguistic Society of the Philippines

sources.note: Comparative wordlist extending the 1974 list (which includes Kinamigin); could carry more Kinamigin forms, though the 1974 version marks no stress, so a rule statement is unlikely.

sources.note: Lobel is the only linguist known to have documented Kinamiging in the field in the modern era; his Philippine wordlists mark stress systematically, and he could state the pattern directly. No publication on Kinamiging appears in his publication list.
